items.title: Live: Inflation eases more than expected in June
items.description: The big focus locally is the consumer price index and what it will mean for interest rates. Follow the day's events and insights from our business reporters on the ABC News live markets blog.

items.title: Live: Ken Henry says decades of climate policy at risk from both left and right
items.description: Former treasury secretary Ken Henry says decades of climate policy is at risk from both the left and right sides of politics. Follow live.

items.title: Taylor denies giving money to group at centre of NSW corruption probe
items.description: The NSW Independent Commission Against Corruption has seen a series of text messages in which key figures discuss a plan to "shake down" Angus Taylor for financial support.

items.title: 'They are getting fooled': How ultra-processed food is made to look healthier
items.description: Industry insiders reveal how Australians are being deceived by marketing and labelling that makes ultra-processed foods appear healthier than they really are.

items.title: Live: Allan, Andrews should appear at royal commission, former IBAC boss says
items.description: Questions are swirling around the details of Ben Carroll's freshly announced royal commission into the construction sector, as the new Victorian premier starts his first full day in the job.

items.title: Local transmission of H5 bird flu 'very, very likely', SA government says
items.description: A further 11 suspected cases of H5 bird flu have been detected in South Australia’s south-east and Kangaroo Island.

items.title: Live: Death toll climbs to 13 after Japan earthquake as rescue efforts continue
items.description: Authorities are scouring the wreckage of a collapsed shopping centre southern Japan following a magnitude-7.1 earthquake. Follow live.

items.title: 'Australia's Banksy' rape case witness wants the courts to hear this
items.description: A woman who accused street artist Anthony Lister of rape is speaking up to help others navigate the police and court systems. Lister was acquitted of all charges last year.

items.title: Home loan borrowers missing out on millions in offset savings
items.description: The corporate regulator found Australian banks paid more than $55 million in compensation in just two years, for failures with mortgage offset accounts, warning customers could be paying more interest than they should.

items.title: Quick hits: Record beaten five times in 10 minutes, pool haka thrills
items.description: New Zealand swimmers pay tribute to a victorious teammate, a lawn bowler fits in some work shifts and a weightlifting record falls a staggering five times. Here are the quick hits from day five of the Commonwealth Games.

items.title: FIFA boss Infantino unveils $20b plan to sell World Cup to Kushner consortium
items.description: FIFA president Gianni Infantino earns more criticism after unveiling a brazen plan to "unleash the commercial potential" of the World Cup.

items.title: Public servant charged over alleged multi-million dollar fraud of NDIS
items.description: A 39-year-old Darwin woman is charged with using her position with the Department of Children and Families to defraud the NDIS of millions of dollars.

items.title: Community in 'shock' amid search for missing boy resuming off SA coast
items.description: The search for a missing three-month-old in SA's South East will resume today, as police continue to investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of the boy's mother and sister. The tragedies have shocked the state and left locals stunned.

items.title: Fresh DNA evidence in 'Echo Point Man' cold case
items.description: Police hope fresh DNA evidence will help them crack a more than two-decades-old cold case in the NSW Blue Mountains.

items.title: Miles Franklin shortlist defies 'shaggy' trend in Australian publishing
items.description: A 'bonkers' zombie novel and a 130-page novella are among six titles vying for Australia's biggest book prize, worth $60,000.

items.title: Australians are the villains in star-studded New Zealand spy comedy
items.description: What happens when you take the exciting world of spies and subterfuge to 1970s New Zealand? We talk to Paul Williams and Bret McKenzie about making their childhood fantasies come true in hilarious new comedy.

items.title: Quiz: 10 travel questions, now boarding at Gate 5
items.description: Which NSW town was the movie Babe filmed in? And where would you find the Atlas Mountains?

items.title: PM's data centre plan may hit roadblock as energy debate heats up
items.description: As two energy ministers oppose the prime minister's plan for national AI rules for data centres, the question over how to power the facilities intensifies.

items.title: Angus Taylor likes to talk about systems. People are his 'kryptonite'
items.description: In an interview for Kitchen Cabinet, the opposition leader recalls feeling a sense of overwhelm and reverence for the parliament when first he took his seat there.

items.title: New Pacific aid map shows 'striking' shift away from China
items.description: Australia supplants China as the dominant lender and infrastructure investor across the Pacific as the government ploughs billions of dollars into the region through both foreign aid and loans.

items.title: Hundreds of Queensland social housing tenants evicted after review
items.description: Dozens of households have been kicked out of social housing in Queensland after being found to own property or earn more than $80,000 a year.

items.title: Gold Coast nurse with rare disorder awaiting third kidney transplant
items.description: Born with congenital nephrotic syndrome of the Finnish type, Daniel Hoepner received his first kidney transplant at six and a second about 16 years later after it failed. Now in his 30s, he faces the same battle again.

items.title: Hospital defends treatment of man later shot by police
items.description: Police detained a 28-year-old man under an emergency mental health order the night before he was shot by officers. The hospital chief executive says a review found he received the appropriate care.

items.title: Queensland nightlife tsar recommends liquor law overhaul
items.description: The government says changes to Christmas and Easter trading are off the table, as Queensland prepared to reinvigorate its nightlife ahead of the 2032 Olympic and Paralympic Games.

items.title: Queensland plan to send youth offenders to boot camps scrutinised
items.description: Advocates have urged the Crisafulli government to reconsider controversial legislation that would send youth offenders to boot camps, warning that any physical and psychological abuse may never come to light due to a "reasonable excuse" provision.
